oracles.title: Executor saved Quint replay
oracles.description: Replay the nine saved Quint scenarios against the Rust executor.
limits: Two interfaces and four scalar operations; sampled evidence, not a proof.
No Linux transport, IPv4 address cascades or cancellation during awaits.
runtime: Rust dependencies/toolchain must be available; Cargo may download dependencies.
effects: Builds Rust test artifacts and retains a private temporary evidence directory.

evidence.location: Printed as Quint artifacts; summary.json contains paths, outcome and actual replay counts.
evidence.success: Exit 0 and summary outcome passed; a valid completion receipt and nonzero saved/generated counts as applicable are required.

task_context.manifest: Retain a pinned task manifest beside the existing evidence; this runner does not yet record the link automatically.
task_context.identity: Manifest id identifies pinned context; SHA256 identifies exact retained file bytes. Oracle ID identifies the selected check, not its verdict.
limits: External provenance only; no task-manifest environment variable is promised by this runner.
Keep existing summary/receipt/observation evidence and its original outcome.

oracles.title: Linux transition measure
oracles.description: Measure state and connectivity before and after one network action.
limits: Namespaces isolate network state, not the host filesystem.
Peer/conntrack state can be absent from capture; ceiling cases expose this limit.
Cases without expectations check reproducibility only; measurements are not independent expected outcomes.
runtime: Unprivileged user and network namespaces must be enabled.
Case-specific commands and kernel support must be available.
Cases with a peer also require ping and sleep for connectivity probes and peer namespaces.

case.description: Explicit case filename stem from nm-transitions list --json

output.description: Directory for JSONL; successful runs replace files of the same name

effects: Runs case setup/actions and connectivity probes in temporary network namespaces.
Replaces successful case JSONL files in the selected output directory.

evidence.success: Exit 0 confirms measurement completed; inspect measured labels and action exit status.

oracles.title: Backend Linux acceptance in a disposable VM
oracles.description: Check the public backend API against independently observed Linux state in a disposable VM.
limits: Run both backend test modules: 22 cases in the current suite.
Outcome-unknown writes and injected malformed responses require separate controlled tests.
Guest pytest invocation requires prior build, deployment and an owned disposable VM.
runtime: Guest: root, Python, pytest, iproute2, sysctl, setpriv, systemd-detect-virt.
Guest: namespaces, veth, bridge, dummy and VLAN kernel support.
Use the testvm lease workflow; deploy suite and explicit probe, snapshot/restore through vm-test and retain evidence outside the guest.

guest_checkout.description: Deployed netfyr checkout inside the guest

guest_probe.description: Explicit deployed backend-probe executable inside the guest

guest_results.description: Guest JUnit path to collect before rollback

effects: Changes guest network namespaces; outer VM workflow may install, deploy and restore a snapshot.

evidence.location: Collect results outside the VM before rollback.
evidence.success: Both modules must execute with no skipped/empty selection; inspect JUnit, probe identity and independent kernel assertions.

task_context.manifest: Optional absolute pinned SpecDoc task manifest; vm-test -m retains unchanged task.manifest.json before VM contact.
task_context.identity: Manifest id identifies pinned context; SHA256 identifies exact retained file bytes. Oracle ID identifies the selected check, not its verdict.
limits: A context manifest does not establish conformance or test success.
vm-test validates identity and structure before contact; source Git authority/completeness must be checked separately.
